_comment: Configuration for the integration test host (IntegrationTestFactory uses
UseEnvironment("Testing")). The same file innovayse-main carries, for the same
reason.
Both values below are read eagerly, while Program.cs is still composing the
builder: it reads Auth:Mode before AddInnovayseAuth, and hands the configuration
to AddInfrastructure, which reads EncryptionKey. WebApplicationFactory merges its
own sources in afterwards, so a value supplied through ConfigureAppConfiguration
arrives too late to be seen — that is what made all 41 tests report "the entry
point exited without ever building an IHost". appsettings.{Environment}.json is
part of WebApplicationBuilder's own defaults, which is early enough.
The factory currently also sets both through UseSetting, which writes host
configuration and wins over this file. That is deliberate belt and braces while
this file is new: once a green run confirms the file is picked up, those two
UseSetting lines are the ones to delete, not these.
Auth:Mode is local because every test here creates its users through
POST /api/auth/register, and LocalAuthController 404s that action in any other
mode. The connection string is deliberately absent: Testcontainers assigns a
random port, so the factory supplies it at runtime — that one works through the
in-memory source because AddDbContext reads configuration inside a deferred
lambda.
The key is a throwaway. It encrypts nothing that outlives the test container,
and it is a real key rather than an exemption so the tests exercise the same
encrypting EF converters production uses.
